If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content: "108 :     public void addObservedPoint(double weight, double x, double y) {\n109 :         observations.add(new WeightedObservedPoint(weight, x, y));\n110 :     }"

Diagnosis:
The test `testLargeSample` fails likely due to memory exhaustion or performance problems when fitting large samples using PolynomialFitter with the new multivariate vector optimizers. From the current bug report, the issue is that when using a large number of weights with these optimizers, an nxn full matrix is created and copied, which causes excessive memory usage. The test generates a large sample size (40000 points) and uses a polynomial fitter to fit the data.

In the code, the method `PolynomialFitter.fit(double[] guess)` is called which forwards to `fit(ParametricUnivariateFunction, double[])`. The `addObservedPoint(double weight, double x, double y)` method adds points of type `WeightedObservedPoint` to a list of observations. The weight parameter given is always 1.0 in the test.

The issue arises inside the optimizer used by `PolynomialFitter` when fitting many observed points. The current multivariate vector optimizers, when weights are supplied as vectors, build an nxn full matrix internally which consumes a lot of memory and leads to exhaustion with large n (points).

This bug explains why this test fails when using large samples because the optimizer backend cannot handle the scale of data due to the full matrix representation of weights. It is also consistent with the bug report's comment that this happens with large point sets even for low polynomial degrees.

Recent bug reports are not directly relevant here. The root cause is that the current multivariate vector optimizers do not support efficiently handling large numbers of weights without generating large matrices, leading to memory problems.

To summarize:
- The test tries to fit polynomials with a large number of points.
- PolynomialFitter uses WeightedObservedPoints and calls optimizers.
- The optimizers create full nxn matrices for weights vectors, causing memory overload.
- This leads to the test failure likely due to out-of-memory or long execution times.
- The crux is inefficiency in weight handling in the vector optimizers used by PolynomialFitter.fit().

This diagnosis relies on the test, the code inspected illustrating method chain, and the current bug report describing the memory problem caused by weight matrix creation in multivariate vector optimizers for large points sets.

Next, it would be helpful to look at the specific optimizer used by PolynomialFitter, i.e., the LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer, especially how it handles weights and observations internally.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
